text:
kevin: quick heads-up — after flipping default to FAv3 kernels on the staging pool we saw a surprising p95 regression for short seq workloads (seq<=32) on A100s. baseline was ~18ms p95, now ~32ms. has anyone else seen this?

maya: saw the same on a small qps test earlier. throughput looked fine but tail spiked. i assumed workspace allocation changes caused extra memcpy.

jon: can you paste the perf dump? curious about batch sizes and whether we fell back to a slower path.

kevin: yup. here's a small snippet from the perf logger for the endpoint:

```
model: gpt-medium-quant
kernel: flashattn_v3
seq: 16
batch: 8
avg_token_ms: 0.9
p50_latency_ms: 12.4
p95_latency_ms: 31.8
workspace_alloc: 48MB -> 120MB
fallbacks: 0
```

kevin: note the workspace jump — FAv3 seems to request a bigger workspace for same config compared to FAv2.

sophie: that aligns with the kernel behavior doc — v3 trades more precomputed state in workspace to avoid recompute. good for long seqs but can hurt short-seq bursty requests due to allocation overhead.

devx: @kevin did you run with our workspace_pool enabled? pool avoids mallocs for each request.

kevin: yes pool=true. but pool size was low (default). i increased pool to 512MB and reran — p95 dropped to ~19ms. so pool sizing is the main lever here.

jon: interesting. so default pool sizing + FAv3 workspace growth => contention and extra GC-like stalls. we should make kernel selection consider effective workspace usage.

maya: we also saw increased CUDA mem fragmentation when many small inferences hit simultaneously. FAv3's larger workspace per stream increases fragmentation risk.

sophie: proposal: runtime kernel selection heuristic should include (seq_len, batch, avg_concurrency, workspace_delta). if workspace_delta>X and seq<=Y pick FAv2. otherwise FAv3. also expose pool sizing alert to Console.

devx: +1. add an autosuggest: when users pick FAv3, show recommended workspace_pool_min based on their seq distribution. saves us support tickets.

jon: another quick idea — if batch<16 and seq<32, enable a lightweight short-seq kernel path (either FAv2 or our small-seq opt) at runtime without full workspace allocation. we already have a small optimization in codebase, can wire toggle to runtime selector.

kevin: agreed. i'll draft a follow-up RFC with numbers and a small experiment matrix (seq: 8/16/32, batch:1/8/16, concurrency: 1/8/32) comparing FAv2/FAv3/patched-shortseq.

maya: add test for quantized vs fp16 models too — quantization can change workspace math and may flip heuristics.

infra-bot: deploy:kernel-selector-experiments started by kevin — env=staging, canary=3 nodes, start=1758207900

kevin: thanks. will share perf dashboards once experiments finish. til then — rolling FAv3 default back on prod or keep?

sophie: keep default flip paused for production until RFC + autosuggest is in. small teams will be bitten otherwise. :+1:

jon: i'll add a note to the rollout checklist to monitor workspace_pool_alloc and cuda_mem_frag metrics for 48h after flip.

kevin: good call. thanks everyone.
